object_description: single-storey addition with a gradated head structure
design_condition: The building completes the campus square along the southern edge, follows existing terrace levels, and uses topographic adjustment to form a central open space.

positive.statement: The proposal interlocks with the existing structure like a missing fitting piece.

position.rationale: Southern-edge massing is visible; the existing structure and interlock are inferred at the campus-facing connection.

positive.statement: The vertical settlement is convincing and creates an orthogonal open space as the campus heart.

position.rationale: The top view identifies a central opening, while elevations show its low position within the settled massing.

negative.statement: The combination of spaces is not yet convincing in terms of composition, and the break area is too dispersed for its needs.

position.rationale: Interior break-space distribution is not visible; the estimate uses the lower southern-facing campus zone.

negative.statement: Access to the adjacent institution from the new campus centre is inadequately formulated and does not seem natural or inviting.

position.rationale: The access route is unmarked, so it is anchored at the likely southern campus-centre threshold.

negative.statement: The central gesture reduces existing outdoor areas and sacrifices important mature trees, while the new tree groups weaken the intended connection.

position.rationale: Landscape elements are absent; the marker covers the central and southern outdoor interface.

negative.statement: The variety of outdoor-space qualities leads to confusion, and the potential of the roof areas is not developed.

position.rationale: Visible roof footprints support an approximate upper eastern placement; outdoor-space qualities remain indistinguishable.

negative.statement: The basement floor has clear organizational and spatial deficiencies and needs a clearer structure.

position.rationale: The basement is not exposed, so the estimate follows the low southern-western building surface.

negative.statement: The gradated head structure is questioned because its sculptural gesture is explained only by apartment sizes and room counts.

position.rationale: The tall stepped head is clearly differentiated on the eastern side across top and elevation views.

negative.statement: The facade relief and its proposed cladding are difficult to understand, and the building reads more as solid construction than as the described hybrid system.

position.rationale: The eastern and northern envelope surfaces are visible, but relief and cladding articulation are not separately resolved.
